title: How MyTeksi Began With One Taxi Company and a Room Without Wi-Fi
conflicts: Early money: founders' RM350,000 plus RM150,000 from the government's Cradle Fund (Digital News Asia 2012) vs business-school capital and Tan's 'whole bank account' (CNBC 2014) vs prize money plus his mother as first individual investor (CNBC Make It 2024); compatible, all given. Founders: DNA (2012) mentions 'three Malaysians' and a 'founding trio' without naming the third and calls Chew Wei Chuan and Aaron Gill co-founders; story names the two Tans as originators and Chew and Gill as co-founders brought in. Office: small room without air conditioning or wi-fi (Make It) vs 'cramped garage' (SCMP via NST). Contest: 'second prize' (DNA) vs 'runners-up' (CNBC), same thing.
notes: Funding changed from the slate's venture to mixed: the start was founders' and family money, a $25,000 prize and a government grant; venture rounds (Vertex, GGV) came later. A widely repeated claim that Tan knocked on taxi windows to sign drivers could not be confirmed from a loadable source and is not used. Laozi chapter 63 was considered but section 3 is already used in another edition, so chapter 9 is used instead. Stance 'challenges'.
